lines: Many people believe that color is something real in objects or in the light they reflect.
For example, they say leaves are green because they reflect green light.
Just like the leaves are real, the green color is real, too.
However, other people say that color is not actually in objects but in our brains.
They think that if no one sees a tree, its leaves have no color.
Nothing would have color if no one looked at it.
In this view, color is not real—it exists only in the brains of people.
Color is real and not real.
As Paul Cézanne, a famous French painter, said, color is “the place where our brains and the world meet.”
Light from the world enters our eyes, and the brain understands it as color.
body.text: Many people believe that color is something real in objects or in the light they reflect. For example, they say leaves are green because they reflect green light. Just like the leaves are real, the green color is real, too. However, other people say that color is not actually in objects but in our brains. They think that if no one sees a tree, its leaves have no color. Nothing would have color if no one looked at it. In this view, color is not real—it exists only in the brains of people. Both ideas are partly true. Color is real and not real. As Paul Cézanne, a famous French painter, said, color is “the place where our brains and the world meet.” Light from the world enters our eyes, and the brain understands it as color.
